title: A height-one valuation ring admits a real absolute value
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $V\subset F$ a valuation subring [def-trf-valuation-ring], with $F$ its fraction field. Suppose that $V$ is not a field and its only prime ideals are $(0)$ and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Then there is a function $|\cdot|:F\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ with $|x|=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $|1|=1$, $|xy|=|x||y|$ and $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$, such that $V=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ and $\mathfrak m=\{x:|x|<1\}$. This absolute value is nontrivial.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp. 6–7: valuation rings, prime ideals and convex subgroups; the height-one/real-valued bridge used at Theorem 3.5.5 Step 3.

proof.text: Put $\Gamma=F^\times/V^\times$, write its multiplication additively, and put $v(x)=[x]$. Define $v(x)\le v(y)$ iff $y/x\in V$. Multiplying $x,y$ by units does not change this condition; transitivity follows from multiplication in $V$, antisymmetry from $y/x$ and its inverse both lying in $V$. The alternative in [def-trf-valuation-ring] gives totality, and replacing $x,y$ by $xz,yz$ gives translation invariance. Thus $\Gamma$ is a totally ordered abelian group and $v(xy)=v(x)+v(y)$. Moreover $v(x)\ge0$ iff $x\in V$, and $v(x)=0$ iff $x\in V^\times$, for $x\ne0$.

source.place: §2.1, printed p. 7, value-group convention and prime/convex-subgroup correspondence; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.3953. The additive construction is written by the worker.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-valuation-prime-convex-correspondence], prime ideals of $V$ are order anti-isomorphic to convex subgroups of this same ordered quotient $\Gamma$. Our hypothesis gives exactly two primes, since $V$ is not a field and hence its maximal ideal is nonzero. Consequently $\Gamma$ has exactly two convex subgroups, namely $\{0\}$ and $\Gamma$, and no proper nonzero convex subgroup.

source.place: §2.1, printed p. 7, value-group convention and prime/convex-subgroup correspondence; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.3953. The additive construction is written by the worker.

proof.text: Fix $\delta>0$ and form $H=\{g\in\Gamma:-n\delta\le g\le n\delta\text{ for some }n\in\mathbf N\}$. This is a subgroup: $0$ has bound $0$, negation preserves a bound, and bounds $n,m$ add to a bound $n+m$. It is convex, since an element between two bounded elements has a bound given by the larger of their bounds. It contains $\delta\ne0$, so Step 2 forces $H=\Gamma$. Thus every $a\in\Gamma$ satisfies $a\le n\delta$ for some $n\in\mathbf N$, exactly the Archimedean condition. This is the elementary bounded-subgroup argument, not an additional valuation-ring lemma.

source.place: §2.1, printed p. 7, value-group convention and prime/convex-subgroup correspondence; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.3953. The additive construction is written by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-archimedean-group-real-embedding] to $\Gamma$, which has the ordered additive group structure of Step 1 and the Archimedean property of Step 3. Obtain an injective monotone additive map $e:\Gamma\to\mathbf R$. It reflects order: if $a>b$, monotonicity gives $e(a)\ge e(b)$ and injectivity excludes equality, so $e(a)>e(b)$.

Define $|0|=0$ and $|x|=\exp(-e(v(x)))$ for $x
e0$. These are nonnegative real numbers. The elementary real exponential identities $\exp(0)=1$, $\exp(s+t)=\exp(s)\exp(t)$ and $\exp(t)>0$ give $|1|=1$, $|x|>0$ for $x
e0$, and $|xy|=|x||y|$ when $x,y
e0$, using $v(xy)=v(x)+v(y)$ and additivity of $e$. If a factor is zero, the same multiplicative equality is $0=0$.

source.place: §2.1, printed p. 7, value-group convention and prime/convex-subgroup correspondence; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.3953. The additive construction is written by the worker.

proof.text: For the strong triangle inequality, zero summands and $x+y=0$ are immediate from nonnegativity. Otherwise interchange $x,y$ if needed so that $v(x)\le v(y)$. Then $y/x\in V$, whence $1+y/x\in V$ and $v(x+y)-v(x)=v(1+y/x)\ge0$. Monotonicity of $e$ and the exponential gives $|x+y|\le |x|$, while $v(x)\le v(y)$ gives $|y|\le |x|$. Thus $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$.

source.place: §2.1, printed p. 7, value-group convention and prime/convex-subgroup correspondence; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.3953. The additive construction is written by the worker.

proof.text: For nonzero $x$, strict monotonicity of the real exponential and order reflection of $e$ give $|x|\le1\iff v(x)\ge0\iff x\in V$ and $|x|<1\iff v(x)>0$. Put $P=\{0\}\cup\{x\in F^\times:v(x)>0\}$. This is a proper ideal of $V$: sums remain positive by the valuation inequality proved in Step 6 (unless zero), negatives have the same value since $-1$ is a unit, and multiplying by an element of $V$ adds a nonnegative value. Every nonzero element of $V\setminus P$ has value zero and is a unit by Step 1. Thus $\mathfrak m\subseteq P$, since a proper ideal contains no unit; maximality and properness of $P$ give $\mathfrak m=P$. At $x=0$, both ball identifications hold since $0\in\mathfrak m\subset V$ and $|0|=0<1$.

source.place: §2.1, printed p. 7, value-group convention and prime/convex-subgroup correspondence; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.3953. The additive construction is written by the worker.

proof.text: To see nontriviality explicitly, choose $z\in F\setminus V$; it is nonzero, and [def-trf-valuation-ring] gives $\pi=z^{-1}\in V$. This $\pi$ is nonzero and not a unit of $V$, since its inverse $z$ is outside $V$. Hence $v(\pi)>0$ and $0<|\pi|<1$.
